summary: Bounds-checked reader that copies three 3-vector (three dword) values from an indexed array into the optional output pointers a3/a4/a5. Guarded by a2 < this[72] (element count); each 36-byte entry at this[73] + 36*a2 holds three 16-bit sub-indices and a base pointer used to reach a 48-byte-stride transform array. Returns a5 when in bounds, otherwise the untouched a2.

operations.description: Guard on a2 < this[72] (element count at this+0x120); when it fails, all output pointers are left unchanged and a2 is returned.
Locate the indexed entry v6 = this[73] + 36*a2; the entry supplies three WORD sub-indices and a DWORD base pointer.
Resolve the transform element for the first sub-index: address = *(*(v6+2*4) + 12) + 48 * v6[0], a 48-byte-stride array access.
Guard on output pointer a3 being non-null.
Copy three dwords (one vector) from the first resolved element into a3[0..2].
Resolve the transform element for the second sub-index v6[1] using the same base pointer and 48-byte stride.
Guard on output pointer a4 being non-null.
Copy three dwords (one vector) from the second resolved element into a4[0..2].
Resolve the transform element for the third sub-index v6[2] using the same base pointer and 48-byte stride.
Guard on output pointer a5 being non-null.
Copy three dwords (one vector) from the third resolved element into a5[0..2].
Return a5 when the outer bounds guard passed (the return value was set to a5), otherwise the original a2.

clean_pseudocode: void* sub_54E1A0(int* this, int index, int* out1, int* out2, int* out3) {
if (out1) { int* p = (int*)(base + 48*entry[0]); out1[0]=p[0]; out1[1]=p[1]; out1[2]=p[2]; }
if (out2) { int* p = (int*)(base + 48*entry[1]); out2[0]=p[0]; out2[1]=p[1]; out2[2]=p[2]; }
if (out3) { int* p = (int*)(base + 48*entry[2]); out3[0]=p[0]; out3[1]=p[1]; out3[2]=p[2]; }
